facts.text: In June 2021 the European Union approved the yellow mealworm as its first insect food.
The approved product was dried yellow mealworm, the larva of the beetle Tenebrio molitor.
Foods containing mealworms must carry labels warning that they may cause allergic reactions.
People who are allergic to crustaceans such as shrimp and crab, or to dust mites, may react to mealworms.
Dried mealworms can be eaten whole as a snack or ground into a powder used in foods such as biscuits and pasta.
Insects are rich in protein, fat and minerals.
Pigs produce 10 to 100 times more greenhouse gases per kilogram than mealworms.
Farming insects uses much less water and land than raising livestock.
Insects are part of the traditional diet of about 2 billion people, and about 1,900 insect species are eaten.
In the EU, insect foods remain a very small niche market.
Crickets are farmed and commonly eaten in Thailand.
